title: The Ampère Lab
summary: Use Ampère’s law for long wires, thick wires, a neutral point, a solenoid and a toroid.
subject: physics
concepts: Field of a long straight wire
Field inside and outside a thick wire
learningOutcome: The student can use Ampère’s law to find the field of long wires, inside and outside a current-carrying wire, a solenoid and a toroid, and locate the neutral point between two wires.

levels.title: A long wire
levels.adds: Baseline: B = μ₀I/2πr with the field circling the wire by the right-hand grip rule (Ex 4.2, 4.3, 4.4).
hints: B = μ₀I/2πr = 2 × 10⁻⁷ I/r with r in metres.
The field is at right angles to the line from the wire to the point.
Right-hand grip: thumb along the current, fingers show the way the field circles.

levels.title: Inside the wire
levels.adds: New idea: inside a wire carrying a uniform current only the enclosed part of the current counts (Example 4.7).
hints: Outside, the Amperian circle encloses all of the current.
Inside, the enclosed current is I r²/a².
B grows in proportion to r inside, and falls as 1/r outside.

levels.title: The null point
levels.adds: More steps: superpose the fields of two wires and find where they cancel.
hints: Slide the probe and watch the net field change sign.
At the neutral point the two fields are equal in size and opposite in direction.
The neutral point is nearer the wire with the smaller current.

levels.title: The solenoid
levels.adds: New idea: inside a long solenoid B = μ₀nI, with n the turns per unit length (Ex 4.8, Example 4.8).
hints: Count the turns in all the layers, then divide by the length in metres.
B = μ₀nI, with μ₀ = 4π × 10⁻⁷ T m/A.

levels.title: The toroid
levels.adds: Apply it: a toroid is a solenoid bent into a ring, B = μ₀NI/2πr in the winding and zero in the hole (Section 4.7).
hints: Use Ampère's law round a circle at the mean radius, which encloses N times the current.
A circle in the hole encloses no net current.

misconceptions: The field of a straight wire points along the wire
The field inside a current-carrying wire is zero everywhere
The field of a solenoid is strongest outside it
A toroid has a strong field in its hole
